retired.reason: Immutable event shape is checked by DCA-ADV-001
Where a domain service sits inside the domain layer is the team's decision; DCA-ADV-010 keeps the layer itself

Keeping no state for a later request in one instance is an operational requirement - several instances without sticky sessions - that a project chooses, not architecture every application shares; the pattern stays guide and catalog guidance for applications that run that way
A separate segment for the anti-corruption layer is a filing decision, and the selection named three suffixes a project cannot change; the pattern stays guide and catalog guidance
Selected on the sample's own pattern name (Enriched*), which a general rule may not carry; value models are covered by DCA-TAC-008..012 and naming one enriched remains guide and catalog guidance

rules.title: Diagnostic: The rules of the Layered Architecture should be followed
rules.rationale: Traditional layering (application accessed only by incoming adapters) contradicts Ports and Adapters, where outgoing adapters implement application-level output ports; the hexagonal rules cover the intended dependency direction
rules.selects: Informational - selects nothing.
rules.checks: Informational - carries doctrine only. The dependency direction is held by the crate graph and the hexagonal rules.

rules.title: Domain must not have dependencies on Infrastructure
rules.rationale: Domain should not depend on infrastructure concerns (Dependency Inversion Principle)
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = domain, the shared kernel's included.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate with layer = infrastructure or bootstrap. The compiler then refuses every use of such a crate; the graph test refuses the Cargo.toml line.

rules.title: Application Services must only use outbound ports (not infrastructure implementations)
rules.rationale: Application services should only use outbound ports declared as interfaces (port.out), not infrastructure implementation details
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = application.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate with layer = infrastructure or bootstrap, its own context's included.

rules.title: Transaction boundaries belong to the application layer
rules.rationale: Transactions are an application-layer concern - domain and incoming adapters must not manage them
rules.selects: Types and functions in every crate that name the building-block trait TransactionBoundary or one of the configured transaction types (for example a database transaction type).
rules.checks: Each sits in an application crate or in the outgoing module of an adapters crate; wiring is also allowed in a bootstrap or infrastructure crate. A domain crate or an incoming adapter that names one is reported. Rust has no declarative transaction attribute, so there is no annotation selection.

rules.title: No implementation is placed into the building-blocks output-port package
rules.rationale: port.out contains outbound port interfaces (Repository, OutputPort, DomainEventPublisher) shared across all bounded contexts. These must be interfaces to ensure the application layer remains framework-independent and follows the Dependency Inversion Principle. Implementations belong in infrastructure or adapter packages.
rules.selects: Items in the building blocks' port module.
rules.checks: A crate cannot add an item to another crate's module, so the building blocks' output-port module holds what the library declares and nothing a project adds. The rule holds by the language.

rules.title: Diagnostic: classes of a module that sit in no layer
rules.rationale: Every rule written for a layer selects by the layer a class is placed in. A class of a module that sits in none - a mapper or a persistence entity beside the adapter packages, a class whose layer is declared only on its neighbour - is seen by none of them
rules.selects: In a crate that carries a context but no layer (the two-crate form), every top-level module.
rules.checks: Informational - lists every top-level module that is none of domain, application, adapters, api, events and infrastructure, and never fails. In the crate-per-layer form every item sits in a layer by its crate and nothing is listed.

rules.title: Domain must not access Application Services (Onion Architecture - Domain is innermost layer)
rules.rationale: Domain is the innermost layer in onion architecture and should not depend on application services
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = domain.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate with layer = application, its own context's included.

rules.title: The Domain Model should be framework independent and should not use 3rd party libraries when possible
rules.rationale: Domain should be framework-independent (Dependency Inversion Principle)
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = domain, the shared kernel's included.
rules.checks: Its normal dependencies are the building blocks, the shared kernel and the configured allowed crates only (by default none). Dev-dependencies are not counted. cargo-deny can refuse known framework crates workspace-wide; the graph test is the per-crate check.

rules.title: Domain models must not carry prohibited framework derives or attributes
rules.rationale: Domain objects carry no metadata for container management, persistence or transaction coordination
rules.selects: Types in a domain crate: structs, enums and their fields.
rules.checks: No derive and no attribute from the configured framework crates (persistence, web, injection) on the type or its fields. A domain crate that does not depend on such a crate cannot name the derive at all (DCA-ONI-002); the source test holds the case where the project allows the crate in the domain.

rules.title: Classes from the domain should not access port adapters
rules.rationale: Domain should not depend on adapters (ports and adapters pattern)
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = domain.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate with layer = adapters, of any context.

rules.title: Application Services should not access port adapters
rules.rationale: Application services should only depend on domain and outbound ports, not adapters
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = application.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate with layer = adapters, of any context.

rules.title: Controllers and Resources must never access repositories directly
rules.rationale: Controllers must go through use cases (input ports), never directly to repositories
rules.selects: Items in the incoming module of every adapters crate.
rules.checks: No item names a trait that carries the repository role or a type that implements one. Other output ports are not checked.

rules.title: Incoming Adapters must only use outbound ports (not infrastructure implementations)
rules.rationale: Incoming adapters should only use outbound ports declared as interfaces (port.out), not infrastructure implementation details
rules.selects: The incoming module of every adapters crate.
rules.checks: No item names a path into a crate with layer = infrastructure or bootstrap. The graph test refuses the dependency where the whole adapters crate must not have it; the source test refuses the use in the incoming module where the outgoing module may.

rules.title: Outgoing adapters must not use another module's infrastructure
rules.rationale: Technical infrastructure reuse preserves module isolation
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = adapters.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate with layer = infrastructure of another context.

rules.title: Incoming port adapters must not depend directly on outgoing port adapters within the same context
rules.rationale: Port adapters should communicate through application services, not directly (event consumers are the exception)
rules.selects: Items in the incoming module of every adapters crate, the configured event-consumer submodule excluded.
rules.checks: No item names a path into the outgoing module of the same crate. The compiler cannot hold this: both modules are one crate.

rules.title: Incoming adapters depend on no other module, except event consumers on the events they subscribe to
rules.rationale: An incoming adapter drives its own module only: a controller that needs a sibling's data goes through its own use case, output port and outgoing adapter to the sibling's published api - only a subscription legitimately meets a foreign contract on the incoming side
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = adapters and the items of its incoming module.
rules.checks: The crate depends on no crate of another context except that context's api crate; within the crate, the incoming module names no path into another context's crate, the configured event-consumer submodule excepted.

rules.title: Classes named *Repository must reside in the outgoing adapter package (name-based discovery of unmarked repositories)
rules.rationale: Repository implementations are secondary adapters (outgoing ports)
rules.selects: Structs and enums in every crate whose name ends with Repository.
rules.checks: Each sits in the outgoing module of an adapters crate.

rules.title: Output Ports in application.shared must extend OutputPort
rules.rationale: Top-level interfaces in application.shared are output ports and must extend OutputPort to be part of the port hierarchy. Nested interfaces (e.g. IdentityProvider.Identity) are part of their enclosing port's contract, not ports themselves
rules.selects: Traits in the shared module of every application crate.
rules.checks: Each carries the output-port role, through OutputPort or one of its sub-traits (Repository, Store, the event publishers).

rules.title: Output ports must not reside in the domain layer
rules.rationale: output ports (Repository, Store, OutputPort) are an application-layer concern and must live in application/shared/, not domain/
rules.selects: Traits in every crate that carry the output-port role.
rules.checks: None sits in a domain crate. A domain crate sees the building blocks and could declare one; the compiler does not refuse it.

rules.title: Incoming Adapters must depend on input port interfaces, not on use case classes
rules.rationale: A driving adapter drives the application through its port. Injecting the concrete implementation instead couples the adapter to one realisation of the use case, defeats the Dependency Inversion Principle the port exists for, and makes the adapter untestable without the real use case and everything it depends on
rules.selects: Items in the incoming module of every adapters crate, event consumers included.
rules.checks: No item names a type that implements an input port; naming the input-port trait is what the rule expects. The use case type stays pub because bootstrap constructs it, so visibility cannot hold this.

rules.title: Incoming Adapters must not depend on domain services
rules.rationale: An incoming adapter translates external input, calls an input port and formats its result. Injecting or invoking a domain service bypasses the application boundary; the use case owns that collaboration and puts its outcome into the result. Outgoing adapters are outside this rule - repositories and other driven adapters may construct or reconstitute domain objects while implementing output ports
rules.selects: Items in the incoming module of every adapters crate.
rules.checks: No item names a type that carries the domain-service role.

rules.title: Outgoing Adapters must not depend on input ports
rules.rationale: An outgoing adapter is driven: the application calls it through an output port. One that calls an input port drives the application instead - it is an incoming adapter filed on the wrong side, and the call it makes runs a second use case from inside the first one's outgoing edge
rules.selects: Items in the outgoing module of every adapters crate.
rules.checks: No item names a trait that carries the input-port role or a type that implements one.

rules.title: GET handlers must not drive an input port that takes a command
rules.rationale: A state-changing use case is reached only by an unsafe HTTP method, never by GET. Links, prefetching, crawlers and cross-site navigation issue GET requests on their own; a GET that runs a command changes state nobody asked to change. A handler that names no HTTP method answers GET as well
rules.selects: Handler functions in the incoming module that the configured router preset registers for GET (for example axum's get(...) or an actix #[get] attribute).
rules.checks: No such function calls an input port whose input type is a command (by default a name ending with Command). Without a router preset nothing is selected.

rules.title: Diagnostic: adapters that publish an enum by its member name
rules.rationale: A value an adapter publishes from an enum is spelled explicitly - a code per value on the enum or a mapping in the adapter - never derived from the member's name. Renaming a member is a refactoring inside the code and must not change what a client reads
rules.selects: Format calls in every adapters crate.
rules.checks: Informational - lists every {:?} or to_string() applied to an enum declared in a domain or application crate, and never fails. A serializer that writes the variant name is not seen.

rules.title: Event listeners that drive an input port must run after the commit in their own transaction
rules.rationale: A reaction to an event changes state or performs an external effect through a use case. Run inside the transaction that raised the event, it changes a second aggregate in the first one's transaction, a failure in the reaction rolls back the fact that caused it, and a retry of the request runs the reaction again. A listener that only translates or measures calls output ports and may run in that transaction
rules.selects: Functions in every crate registered as event listener by the configured listener preset.
rules.checks: A listener that calls an input port runs after the commit in its own transaction, as the preset expresses it. Rust has no common listener attribute; without a preset nothing is selected.

rules.title: Controllers must reside in an incoming adapter package
rules.rationale: A controller turns a request into a command or a query and is an incoming adapter. Outside the incoming adapter packages it is outside the selection of every rule written for incoming adapters - the GET-handler rule, the controller naming rules, the boundary rules - and passes them all
rules.selects: Handler functions the configured router preset recognises, anywhere in the workspace.
rules.checks: Each sits in the incoming module of an adapters crate. Rust handlers are functions, not classes.

rules.title: Output port implementations are placed in the outgoing adapters
rules.rationale: An output port is what the application needs from outside; whatever implements it is an outgoing adapter - the implemented port says so. An implementation placed in the infrastructure package, the application, the domain or in no layer at all is outside the selection of every rule written for outgoing adapters, and infrastructure then holds behaviour instead of wiring alone
rules.selects: Every impl of a trait that carries the output-port role.
rules.checks: The implementing type sits in the outgoing module of an adapters crate. The orphan rule already keeps the impl out of the domain crate, which cannot see the application's port; a test double in the application crate is reported.

rules.title: Aggregate Roots must implement AggregateRoot<T, ID>
rules.rationale: Classes named *AggregateRoot must implement AggregateRoot interface (DDD pattern)
rules.selects: Structs in every domain crate whose name ends with AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: The type implements AggregateRoot. Rust names rarely carry the suffix; selection by name stays as in Java.

rules.title: Aggregate Roots must not hold references to Repositories or other Output Ports
rules.rationale: Aggregates are persistence-ignorant: use cases retrieve facts; external calculations belong in domain services over supplied snapshots. Review callback parameters manually; this field check cannot prove semantic responsibility
rules.selects: Types that implement AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: No field type, generic arguments and Box<dyn ...> included, names a trait with the output-port role. The project's own ports live in the application crate, which the domain crate cannot see; the source test holds the building blocks' own port traits.

rules.title: Aggregate Roots must not have fields with other Aggregate Root types
rules.rationale: Vernon's Aggregate Design Rule #3: reference other Aggregates by identity to keep aggregate boundaries and transactional consistency intact
rules.selects: Types that implement AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: No field type, through Vec, Option, Box and other generic arguments, is a type that implements AggregateRoot. References by id pass.

rules.title: Entities must have an ID field
rules.rationale: An Entity is defined by its identity, which is a value object implementing the Id marker
rules.selects: Types that implement Entity, aggregate roots included.
rules.checks: The trait's associated type Id is bound to the Id marker, so the compiler holds the typed identity. The source test checks that a field of that type exists, so the id is state, not computed.

rules.title: Entities must not be instantiated directly from outside the aggregate
rules.rationale: Entities are created through their aggregate root so that the root can enforce its invariants
rules.selects: Types that implement Entity but not AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: The type has no pub field and no pub associated function that returns Self; pub(crate) and private ones pass. With private fields no code outside the aggregate's module can build one by struct literal - the compiler holds that part.

rules.title: Domain model classes must not have public setter methods
rules.rationale: Behavior-rich domain models change state through intention-revealing methods from the ubiquitous language, never through public setters
rules.selects: Types that implement Entity, aggregate roots included.
rules.checks: No pub method named set_<name> takes &mut self and exactly one further parameter and returns ().

rules.title: Entities must not have fields with Aggregate Root types
rules.rationale: An entity inside an aggregate references other aggregates by identity only, otherwise the aggregate boundary leaks
rules.selects: Types that implement Entity but not AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: No field type, through generic arguments, is a type that implements AggregateRoot.

rules.title: Value Objects must not contain Aggregate Roots or Entities
rules.rationale: A Value Object is defined by its attributes; holding an object with identity would give it a lifecycle it must not have
rules.selects: Types that implement Value.
rules.checks: No field type, through generic arguments, is a type that implements Entity or AggregateRoot.

rules.reason: Rust has no inheritance; a struct cannot be extended, so a value object is final by construction.

rules.title: Value Objects must not mutate their state
rules.rationale: Records have implicitly final fields and enums are immutable by design; a hand-written value class must make every instance field final itself
rules.selects: Types that implement Value.
rules.checks: No method takes &mut self, no field is pub, and no field type is an interior-mutability type (Cell, RefCell, Mutex, RwLock, atomics). Rust has no final field; immutability is the absence of a mutating API.

rules.title: Value Objects must not have setter methods
rules.rationale: Value Objects are immutable; state changes produce a new instance instead of mutating
rules.selects: Types that implement Value.
rules.checks: No method is named set_<name>, whatever its receiver.

rules.title: Value Objects must be records or immutable classes with attribute equality
rules.rationale: A record grants attribute-based equality for free; a hand-written Value Object class must override equals and hashCode itself to compare by its attributes
rules.selects: Types that implement Value.
rules.checks: The building-block trait Value has PartialEq as supertrait, so the compiler refuses a value object without equality. Whether the equality compares every attribute is not decidable; a derive is the expected form.

rules.title: Repository Interfaces should extend Repository Marker Interface
rules.rationale: Repository interfaces should extend Repository marker interface
rules.selects: Traits in every application crate whose name ends with Repository.
rules.checks: The trait carries the repository role.

rules.title: Repository interfaces must reside in the application layer (local to a use case or shared)
rules.rationale: Repository interfaces are output ports in the application layer (Hexagonal Architecture)
rules.selects: Traits that carry the repository role, the building block excluded.
rules.checks: Each sits in an application crate, the shared kernel's included.

rules.title: Repository Implementations must reside in adapter.outgoing package
rules.rationale: Repository implementations are outgoing adapters in bounded contexts
rules.selects: Types that implement a trait with the repository role.
rules.checks: Each sits in the outgoing module of an adapters crate.

rules.title: Repositories must only exist for Aggregate Roots
rules.rationale: A repository is the collection of one aggregate type; a repository for an entity would let callers bypass the root that guards the aggregate's invariants
rules.selects: Traits with the repository role whose name ends with Repository.
rules.checks: The bound Repository<T: AggregateRoot> makes a repository for anything but a root unkompilable. The source test checks the name: the trait is named after the type it binds plus Repository.

rules.title: Repository methods must not return non-root Entities
rules.rationale: A caller receiving an Entity that is not an Aggregate Root could mutate part of an aggregate without passing its root, so the root's invariants would never run
rules.selects: Traits with the repository role.
rules.checks: No method of the trait returns a type, through generic arguments, that implements Entity but not AggregateRoot. A pub(crate) entity cannot be named by the application crate at all.

rules.title: Store interfaces must extend the Store marker, not Repository
rules.rationale: Stores extend the Store marker; Repository is reserved for Aggregate Roots
rules.selects: Traits outside adapters and infrastructure crates whose name ends with Store.
rules.checks: The trait carries the store role and not the repository role.

rules.title: Store interfaces must reside in the application layer (local to a use case or shared)
rules.rationale: Store interfaces are output ports in the application layer (Hexagonal Architecture)
rules.selects: Traits that carry the store role, the building block excluded.
rules.checks: Each sits in an application crate.

rules.title: Store implementations must reside in the adapter.outgoing package
rules.rationale: Store implementations are outgoing adapters in bounded contexts
rules.selects: Types that implement a trait with the store role.
rules.checks: Each sits in the outgoing module of an adapters crate.

rules.title: Store interfaces must not declare save or delete methods
rules.rationale: save/delete are Repository semantics; a Store that has them is a Repository wearing the wrong name, and the stored object should then be an Aggregate Root
rules.selects: Traits that carry the store role.
rules.checks: No method declared on the trait itself is named save, delete or delete_by_id.

rules.title: Aggregate Roots must not expose a public struct literal
rules.rationale: An aggregate comes into being in two ways - created as a business fact or reconstituted from storage - and each is a named factory method. A public constructor is a third, unnamed way that skips the creation invariants and the event creation raises
rules.selects: Types that implement AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: No field is pub. Rust has no constructor; the struct literal is the constructor, and private fields keep it inside the aggregate's module. The root's associated functions (create, place, ...) are its factories and check invariants.

rules.title: Value Objects must not declare a neutral factory beside an origin factory with the same parameters
rules.rationale: A value built from input and a value rebuilt from storage are two origins with different checks - validated and derived on the way in, taken as given on the way back - and each has its own named factory. A second factory that takes the same parameters, such as a neutral of(...) beside them, leaves the caller to guess which checks run
rules.selects: Types that implement Value and their pub associated functions returning Self.
rules.checks: No function named new takes the same parameter types, in the same order, as another such function. Two named origins (from_input, from_stored) pass.

rules.title: Domain types must not hold bare primitives, strings or time types; a boolean only as a field or a predicate
rules.rationale: A value with rules of its own - a postal code, a quantity, a moment, an identifier - is a value object; held as a bare String, int, Instant or UUID its validation is repeated at every use or missing. A value object with several components holds value objects too; only a wrapper - a value of exactly one component - holds the primitive it wraps. A single yes/no fact may stay a boolean field: the type is told (complete()) and answers (isCompleted()). A boolean parameter is a flag argument - setCompleted(true) lets the caller set the state instead of triggering the behaviour - and three or more states, or transitions with rules, are an enum or a value
rules.selects: Types, fields and pub signatures in every domain crate, the shared kernel's included. Not selected: a single-field newtype that implements Value or Id, failures, and trait methods of a building block.
rules.checks: No field, parameter or return type, through generic arguments, is String, &str, a primitive, a time type (std::time::SystemTime, chrono, time) or a bare Uuid. A private field of type bool - a single yes/no fact - and a bool return - a predicate - pass; a bool parameter and a pub bool struct field, flag arguments, do not.

rules.title: Diagnostic: Display discovered bounded contexts
rules.rationale: Making the discovered contexts visible shows which packages the strategic rules govern
rules.selects: Every crate whose [package.metadata.dca] carries a context.
rules.checks: Informational - lists each context with its crates and the shared kernel, and never fails.

rules.title: Shared Kernel must not have dependencies on any bounded context
rules.rationale: Shared Kernel must be context-independent — it is shared by all contexts and owned by none
rules.selects: The crate with layer = shared-kernel.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate that carries a context.

rules.title: Modules must not access each other in the application layer
rules.rationale: An application layer talks to other modules through its own output ports, implemented by adapters - never directly. Selects structurally over every module that owns a DCA layer, declared as a bounded context or not: an undeclared module must not be able to escape isolation by staying off the context map
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = application.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate of another context, that context's api crate included.

rules.title: Modules must not access each other in the domain layer
rules.rationale: A domain layer talks to its own module and the shared kernel, nothing else - not even another module's api/. Selects structurally over every module that owns a DCA layer, declared as a bounded context or not
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = domain.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate of another context, that context's api crate included.

rules.title: Open Host Services must be published: in the api package or as an incoming adapter
rules.rationale: An Open Host Service is the protocol a context publishes for other contexts - in-process as its api/ package, over the network as an incoming adapter (REST, gRPC, MCP). It belongs at the context boundary, never in the domain or application layer; the adapter's sub-package is irrelevant
rules.selects: Types that implement the OpenHostService marker.
rules.checks: Each sits in an api crate or in the incoming module of an adapters crate.

rules.title: Outgoing adapters accessing other modules must only use their published api/ and events/ packages
rules.rationale: Cross-module communication goes through the target's published api/ (synchronous) and events/ (asynchronous) packages - DCA's in-process contract convention, package names rather than framework annotations - never through its domain, application, adapter or infrastructure packages. Selects structurally over every module that owns a DCA layer, declared as a bounded context or not
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = adapters.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies on another context name that context's api crate only. A foreign domain, application or adapters crate is refused by the graph test; anything the api crate does not export is refused by the compiler.

rules.title: Integration event contracts reside in the configured events segment
rules.rationale: Integration contracts are published separately from translators and transport adapters
rules.selects: Types that implement IntegrationEvent.
rules.checks: Each sits in the events module of an api crate.

rules.title: Integration Events should have immutable shape
rules.rationale: An integration event is a published contract: once another context has read it, its shape may only grow, never change under an existing reader. A mutable event cannot make that promise - any holder can rewrite what a second consumer will read
rules.selects: Types that implement IntegrationEvent.
rules.checks: No method takes &mut self and no field type is an interior-mutability type.

rules.title: Diagnostic: Event Listeners consuming integration events should use Anti-Corruption Layer
rules.rationale: Consumed integration events are translated into the consuming context's own language before they reach its domain — verified by code review, not statically
rules.selects: Informational - selects nothing.
rules.checks: Nothing is asserted. Whether a consumed integration event is translated before it reaches the domain is a review check.

rules.title: At least one bounded context is declared
rules.rationale: Without a declared context the context-map and isolation rules select nothing and report success over an empty model
rules.selects: The workspace members.
rules.checks: At least one crate carries a context in [package.metadata.dca].

rules.title: At least one module owns a DCA layer
rules.rationale: Without a discovered module root every rule that selects over the layers matches nothing and reports success over an empty model
rules.selects: The workspace members.
rules.checks: At least one crate carries one of the layers in [package.metadata.dca].

rules.title: Interfaces in a module's events package must extend IntegrationEvent
rules.rationale: Everything in the events package is a published event contract. An interface there is one a producer's integration event implements and a consumer receives; delivery is at least once, so the consumer needs the event's identity and occurrence time through that interface, not only the payload
rules.selects: Traits in the events module of every api crate.
rules.checks: Each carries the IntegrationEvent role.

rules.title: Upstream, ExternalUpstream, and Partnership may only be declared on bounded context packages
rules.rationale: Context map declarations are reserved for bounded contexts — only a context can be downstream of, or partner with, another
rules.selects: Every crate's [package.metadata.dca].
rules.checks: upstreams, external-upstreams and partnerships appear only in the metadata of the crate that declares the context (by default its domain crate).

rules.title: ExternalUpstream declarations must be well-formed and unique per name and interaction
rules.rationale: The identity of an @ExternalUpstream declaration is (name, interaction); internal contexts are declared with @Upstream instead
rules.selects: Every external-upstreams entry.
rules.checks: name is not blank and not the name of a context, and (name, interaction) occurs at most once per context.

rules.title: Upstream declarations must reference an existing bounded context and never the declaring context itself
rules.rationale: A dangling or self-referencing upstream edge describes a relationship that cannot exist
rules.selects: Every upstreams entry.
rules.checks: context names an existing context and not the declaring one.

rules.title: Upstream declarations must be unique per context and channel, and via must not be empty
rules.rationale: The identity of an @Upstream declaration is (context, via); different translations per channel require separate annotations
rules.selects: Every upstreams entry.
rules.checks: via holds at least one channel (api, events), and (context, channel) occurs at most once per context.

rules.title: Upstream declarations and the module declaration's allowed dependencies must agree
rules.rationale: Neither the context map nor the module boundary may know more than the other — an edge that exists only on one side is stale
rules.selects: Every context with upstreams entries.
rules.checks: The declared edges equal the Cargo dependencies of the context's crates on another context's api crate. Cargo.toml is the module declaration in Rust; there is no second one to compare.

rules.title: Implemented Upstream declarations must be backed by an actual code dependency
rules.rationale: A declared IMPLEMENTED edge without any real dependency is stale (or premature — then it is PLANNED) and would otherwise pass forever alongside an equally stale module boundary entry
rules.selects: Every implemented upstreams entry.
rules.checks: For each channel, some source file of the declaring context names a path into the target's api crate (api or events module).

rules.title: Anti-Corruption Layer: upstream contract types must stay inside the matching adapter
rules.rationale: The ACL sits where the dependency crosses the boundary — outgoing adapters for synchronous API calls, incoming adapters for consumed events — and translates the upstream contract into the context's own model there
rules.selects: Every upstreams entry with translation = acl.
rules.checks: Only the context's adapters crate depends on the target's api crate; within it, the api channel is named only in the outgoing module and the events channel only in the incoming module.

rules.title: Conformist: upstream contract types must never reach the domain layer
rules.rationale: Conformism does not suspend domain purity — the domain layer stays free of foreign contract types
rules.selects: Every upstreams entry with translation = conformist.
rules.checks: The context's domain crate does not depend on the target's api crate.

rules.title: External system contract types must respect the declared translation and interaction
rules.rationale: An external system's contract types are confined to the adapter where the exchange crosses the boundary (ACL) or at least kept out of the domain (Conformist)
rules.selects: Every external-upstreams entry that names contract crates.
rules.checks: With acl, only the adapters crate depends on a contract crate and only the matching module (outgoing for outbound, incoming for inbound) names it; with conformist, the domain crate does not depend on one.

rules.title: Cross-context dependencies on published interfaces require an Upstream declaration
rules.rationale: Every real dependency on a foreign api/ or events/ package is a context-map edge and must be declared as such
rules.selects: Every Cargo dependency of a context's crate on another context's api crate.
rules.checks: The source context declares an upstreams entry for that context and channel.

rules.title: Partnership declarations must reference an existing bounded context, never themselves, and must be symmetric
rules.rationale: A partnership is a mutual commitment — it exists only when both contexts declare it
rules.selects: Every partnerships entry.
rules.checks: It names an existing context, not itself, and the target declares the partnership back.

rules.title: Diagnostic: Display declared context map
rules.rationale: Printing the declared edges makes the executable context map reviewable at a glance
rules.selects: Every upstreams, external-upstreams and partnerships entry.
rules.checks: Informational - lists every declared edge and never fails.

rules.title: Every allowed dependency of a module declaration must be backed by an actual code dependency
rules.rationale: A context declares only the dependencies it uses. An allowed dependency no class uses is a door left open: the next dependency through it passes the module boundary without anyone deciding it
rules.selects: Every Cargo dependency of a context's crate on another context's crate.
rules.checks: Some source file of the crate names the dependency. The rustc lint unused_crate_dependencies holds the same per crate.

rules.title: Domain Events must implement DomainEvent and have immutable shape
rules.rationale: Domain events should have immutable state implementing DomainEvent (named in past tense, e.g., ProductCreated, CartCleared)
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainEvent.
rules.checks: No method takes &mut self and no field type is an interior-mutability type. Implementing the trait is the selection itself.

rules.title: Domain Events must reside in domain package
rules.rationale: Domain events are part of the domain layer (named in past tense)
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainEvent.
rules.checks: Each sits in a domain crate.

rules.title: Domain events must not carry prohibited framework metadata
rules.rationale: Domain objects carry no metadata for container management, persistence or transaction coordination
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainEvent in a domain crate.
rules.checks: No derive and no attribute from the configured framework crates (persistence, web, injection) on the type or its fields. A domain crate that does not depend on such a crate cannot name the derive at all (DCA-ONI-002); the source test holds the case where the project allows the crate in the domain.

rules.title: Integration Events must be annotated with IntegrationEventType
rules.rationale: @IntegrationEventType(name, version) is the contract identity of every integration event — the serializer keys (name, version) to the class and stamps both onto the wire envelope
rules.selects: Types that implement IntegrationEvent.
rules.checks: The trait requires the associated constants TYPE and VERSION, so the compiler refuses an integration event without its type metadata. Rust has no annotations; the constants are the metadata.

rules.title: Integration events carry the schema version in their type metadata, not in the payload
rules.rationale: The schema version is a class property (@IntegrationEventType), never per-instance payload data — an explicit schema-version data field duplicates the annotation and can drift from it
rules.selects: Types that implement IntegrationEvent.
rules.checks: No field is named schema_version, event_version or contract_version.

rules.title: Domain events that are not integration events carry no schema version
rules.rationale: Versioning is a contract concern of integration events — a purely internal domain event has no wire contract to version
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainEvent but not IntegrationEvent.
rules.checks: No field is named schema_version, event_version or contract_version.

rules.title: Domain Events must have a timestamp field
rules.rationale: An event records something that happened — without a timestamp the fact cannot be ordered, replayed or audited
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainEvent.
rules.checks: The trait requires occurred_at(); the source test checks that a field of one of the configured timestamp types (by default the building blocks' Timestamp) backs it.

rules.title: Marked domain services reside in a module domain
rules.rationale: Domain services are part of the domain layer, not application layer
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainService.
rules.checks: Each sits in a domain crate.

rules.title: Domain services must not carry prohibited framework metadata
rules.rationale: Domain objects carry no metadata for container management, persistence or transaction coordination
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainService in a domain crate.
rules.checks: No derive and no attribute from the configured framework crates (persistence, web, injection) on the type or its fields. A domain crate that does not depend on such a crate cannot name the derive at all (DCA-ONI-002); the source test holds the case where the project allows the crate in the domain.

rules.title: Domain Services should be stateless (only final fields for dependencies)
rules.rationale: Domain services should be stateless (only final fields for dependencies)
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainService.
rules.checks: No method takes &mut self and no field type is an interior-mutability type. Rust has no final field; statelessness is the absence of mutation.

rules.title: Types carrying the factory role are named *Factory
rules.rationale: A factory is found by its role, and read by its name: a type that creates aggregates and is not called one makes the creation site hard to find in review and in a search
rules.selects: Types that implement Factory.
rules.checks: The name ends with Factory.

rules.title: Factories must reside in domain package
rules.rationale: Factories are part of the domain layer (complex aggregate creation logic)
rules.selects: Types that implement Factory.
rules.checks: Each sits in a domain crate.

rules.title: Factories must not carry prohibited framework metadata
rules.rationale: Domain objects carry no metadata for container management, persistence or transaction coordination
rules.selects: Types that implement Factory in a domain crate.
rules.checks: No derive and no attribute from the configured framework crates (persistence, web, injection) on the type or its fields. A domain crate that does not depend on such a crate cannot name the derive at all (DCA-ONI-002); the source test holds the case where the project allows the crate in the domain.

rules.title: Factories should be stateless (only final fields for dependencies)
rules.rationale: Factories should be stateless (only final fields for dependencies)
rules.selects: Types that implement Factory.
rules.checks: No method takes &mut self and no field type is an interior-mutability type.

rules.title: Specifications reside in the domain layer
rules.rationale: A specification is a rule of the model expressed as a predicate; it belongs where the model is, not in the layer that happens to ask the question
rules.selects: Types that implement Specification or whose name ends with Specification.
rules.checks: Each sits in a domain crate.

rules.title: Specifications must not carry prohibited framework metadata
rules.rationale: Domain objects carry no metadata for container management, persistence or transaction coordination
rules.selects: Specifications in a domain crate.
rules.checks: No derive and no attribute from the configured framework crates (persistence, web, injection) on the type or its fields. A domain crate that does not depend on such a crate cannot name the derive at all (DCA-ONI-002); the source test holds the case where the project allows the crate in the domain.

rules.title: Aggregates, entities and value objects must not use domain services
rules.rationale: A domain service exists for logic that spans several aggregates, so the application calls it; a model type that reaches for one would drive another aggregate from inside its own
rules.selects: Methods of types that implement AggregateRoot, Entity or Value.
rules.checks: No method body calls a function of, or constructs, a type that implements DomainService. A parameter of that type alone is not reported.

rules.title: Domain service operations take an aggregate or an entity
rules.rationale: A domain service works on the model itself; an operation that only takes extracted values moves the decision out of the domain and into its caller
rules.selects: pub methods of types that implement DomainService.
rules.checks: At least one parameter is, by value or by reference, a type that implements AggregateRoot or Entity.

rules.title: The base InputPort contract is not redeclared in the project
rules.rationale: Base InputPort interface defines the generic contract for all use cases (Hexagonal Architecture)
rules.selects: Traits named InputPort anywhere in the workspace.
rules.checks: None outside the building blocks.

rules.title: Commands reside in the application layer
rules.rationale: Use case commands should be in application layer (CQRS pattern)
rules.selects: Structs and enums whose name ends with Command.
rules.checks: Each sits in an application crate.

rules.title: Queries reside in the application layer
rules.rationale: Use case queries should be in application layer (CQRS pattern)
rules.selects: Structs and enums whose name ends with Query.
rules.checks: Each sits in an application crate.

rules.title: Use Case Commands should be immutable (final or records)
rules.rationale: Use case commands should be immutable (value objects)
rules.selects: Structs in application crates whose name ends with Command.
rules.checks: No method takes &mut self and no field type is an interior-mutability type.

rules.title: Use Case Queries should be immutable (final or records)
rules.rationale: Use case queries should be immutable (value objects)
rules.selects: Structs in application crates whose name ends with Query.
rules.checks: No method takes &mut self and no field type is an interior-mutability type.

rules.title: Types named *Result reside in the application layer
rules.rationale: Use case result models should be in application layer. Domain Value Objects with 'Result' in name are allowed in domain layer.
rules.selects: Structs and enums whose name ends with Result and that do not implement Value. std's Result is not a declaration and is never selected.
rules.checks: Each sits in an application crate. An enum in a domain crate that a domain operation returns is a domain outcome and is exempt.

rules.title: Use Case Result Models should be immutable (final or records)
rules.rationale: Use case result models should be immutable (value objects)
rules.selects: Structs in application crates whose name ends with Result.
rules.checks: No method takes &mut self and no field type is an interior-mutability type.

rules.title: Types named *Response reside in an adapter
rules.rationale: HTTP response models should be in adapter layer
rules.selects: Structs and enums whose name ends with Response.
rules.checks: Each sits in an adapters crate.

rules.title: Use cases that save an aggregate must publish its domain events
rules.rationale: A saved aggregate must not keep its events: unpublished, they are lost, and stored on the instance they may later be published out of context. Publishing belongs after the save, in the use case that owns the unit of work - unless the aggregate is proven never to register an event: its whole hierarchy is under scan and no code unit of it, of a helper it calls, or of any other scanned class registering on that aggregate (a nested class it never calls) calls registerEvent; a helper in another top-level class cannot reach the protected method; an unresolved type argument keeps the requirement. Checked per entry path, following calls within the use case class: every entry point that reaches a save - a method callable from outside the class, or one nothing in the class calls - must also reach a publication; a wrapper that publishes does not cover a direct call of the public method it wraps, and a helper two methods share does not connect them. That the publication follows the save and concerns the same aggregate is not established statically. Only DomainEventPublisher.publishAndClearEvents counts as a publication: iterating domainEvents() and calling publish(event), even followed by clearDomainEvents(), separates dispatch from acknowledgement and is not accepted
rules.selects: Functions of types that implement an input port.
rules.checks: A function that calls save on a repository also takes the aggregate's events (take_events) and hands them to a DomainEventPublisher, directly or through a function of the same type.

rules.title: DTOs must not be used in the Domain Layer
rules.rationale: Domain layer should not depend on DTOs (presentation concerns) - Dependency Inversion Principle
rules.selects: Items in every domain crate.
rules.checks: No item declares or names a type whose name ends with Dto.

rules.title: DTOs must not be used in the Application Layer
rules.rationale: Application layer should use Command/Query/Response models, not presentation DTOs (Clean Architecture)
rules.selects: Items in every application crate.
rules.checks: No item declares or names a type whose name ends with Dto.

rules.title: Use cases that save an aggregate or publish domain events must have a transaction boundary
rules.rationale: The use case owns the unit of work. Saving an aggregate is one business fact, yet the repository may write it as several statements - an aggregate of entities and value objects often spans several tables - and a repository adapter draws no boundary of its own; without one, a failure between the statements leaves half an aggregate behind. Publishing adds a second effect that must fall with the save: integration events are relayed after commit by the framework's after-commit listeners, and their publication is registered in the publishing transaction. Without an active transaction the after-commit listeners are skipped silently and nothing is registered: the use case succeeds, the other contexts never hear of it. The boundary is either declarative transaction metadata (the configured transactional annotation on the class or the executing method) or an explicit TransactionBoundary.inTransaction(...) around load, mutate, save and publish. Checked per entry path, following calls within the class: from every entry point - a method callable from outside the class, or one nothing in the class calls - no route down to the saving, deleting or publishing method may be free of an annotation or a boundary; a covered caller does not cover another route to the same helper, and a boundary on one route does not cover a second route. Whether the save or the publication sits inside the block handed to inTransaction(...) is not visible in ArchUnit's call model, which folds a lambda's body into the enclosing method; that placement stays a review check
rules.selects: Functions of types that implement an input port.
rules.checks: A function that calls save or delete on a repository or a DomainEventPublisher does so inside the closure it passes to TransactionBoundary (or a function of the same type that does). Rust has no transactional attribute; the explicit boundary is the only form.

rules.reason: Rust has no declarative transaction attribute; the boundary is the explicit TransactionBoundary port, which DCA-USE-012 reads, and the rule selects only declaratively transactional use cases.

rules.title: Use case packages within a module must use one consistent depth (flat or grouped by feature)
rules.rationale: A use case package sits either directly below the application package (application.<usecase>) or one level deeper inside a feature (application.<feature>.<usecase>). A feature is an optional, domain-named group of related use cases - a navigation boundary inside one bounded context, not a layer, module or aggregate owner. Mixing both forms in one module makes it unclear whether a package is a feature, a use case or a leftover; nesting deeper than a feature hides the use case. The rule checks legibility only: it does not infer bounded contexts, feature semantics or aggregate ownership. application.shared holds the context-wide output ports and is not a use case package
rules.selects: Types that implement an input port in every application crate, the shared module excluded.
rules.checks: All sit at one module depth: application::<use_case> or application::<feature>::<use_case>.

rules.title: Use Case Result Models must not expose aggregate roots or entities
rules.rationale: A result is the use case's answer, not a handle on the model: identity and behaviour stay behind the port; values, enriched models and read models may cross. Checked transitively through nested records, part records anywhere in the application layer (application.shared included), generic type arguments (List<T>, Optional<T>, Map<K,V>) and inherited fields, a generic base class's type parameters resolved as the result binds them
rules.selects: Structs in application crates whose name ends with Result.
rules.checks: No field type, through generic arguments and into other application structs, implements AggregateRoot or Entity.

rules.title: Use cases must not invoke other use cases
rules.rationale: Ordinary operations do not coordinate other operations; coordination requires explicit transaction and failure semantics
rules.selects: Types that implement an input port.
rules.checks: No field, parameter or generic bound names another input-port trait or a type that implements one.

rules.title: Use cases expose no public operation outside their input port
rules.rationale: The input port describes the complete externally callable operation surface
rules.selects: Types that implement an input port.
rules.checks: No pub inherent method other than an associated function that returns Self (the constructor bootstrap calls). The operation lives in the input-port impl.

rules.title: In a module grouped by feature, incoming adapters must drive the commands of one feature only
rules.rationale: Once the application is grouped, the incoming adapter is cut the same way: one controller changes state through the use cases of one feature. A class that drives the commands of two features grows with every use case of both and hides the cut the application already made. Reading a neighbouring feature's query is no reason to cut
rules.selects: Items in the incoming module of an adapters crate whose application groups use cases by feature.
rules.checks: The input ports taking a command that an item names belong to at most one feature.

rules.title: Query use cases must not write or publish
rules.rationale: A read never creates. A query has no side effect: it does not create, save or publish, and when nothing exists it answers none. Find-or-create is a command, called where the caller is about to change state; a page or an answer that only shows what exists asks the query
rules.selects: Types that implement an input port whose input is a query.
rules.checks: No function calls a write (save, delete, remove, add, insert, update, ...) on a repository or store, nor an event publisher.

rules.title: Use cases must not parse raw input into an id
rules.rationale: The adapter turns raw input into the types the input port takes: an id arrives as the id's value type, parsed at the edge or by the value type's own factory, never as text the use case parses. Text that does not parse is a malformed call the adapter answers itself; the use case never sees it
rules.selects: Every application crate.
rules.checks: clippy.toml lists uuid::Uuid::parse_str and uuid::Uuid::from_str under disallowed-methods. Parsing happens in the adapter or in the id's own constructor.

rules.title: Application layer InputPort implementations must end with 'UseCase'
rules.rationale: InputPort implementations (use cases) should follow consistent naming conventions (Hexagonal Architecture)
rules.selects: Types in application crates that implement an input port.
rules.checks: The name ends with UseCase.

rules.reason: Rust has no injectable stereotype attribute; bootstrap constructs use cases in code, so there is nothing to list.

rules.title: InputPort interfaces must end with 'InputPort'
rules.rationale: Input port interfaces should follow consistent naming conventions (Hexagonal Architecture)
rules.selects: Traits in application crates that carry the input-port role, InputPort itself excluded.
rules.checks: The name ends with InputPort.

rules.title: Repository Interfaces must end with 'Repository' (name-based discovery)
rules.rationale: Repository interfaces should follow consistent naming conventions (DDD pattern)
rules.selects: Traits in application crates whose name contains Repository.
rules.checks: The name ends with Repository.

rules.reason: Rust web handlers are free functions, not controller classes; the module that holds them carries the name, and DCA-HEX-018 places it.
Rust web handlers are free functions, not resource classes; the module that holds them carries the name, and DCA-HEX-018 places it.

rules.title: DTOs must reside in the adapter layer, not in domain or application
rules.rationale: DTOs are adapter concerns (presentation or external API) - not in domain or application
rules.selects: Structs and enums whose name ends with Dto.
rules.checks: Each sits in an adapters crate.

rules.title: Converters must reside in the adapter layer
rules.rationale: Converters/Mappers translate between layers and should be in adapters
rules.selects: Structs and enums whose name ends with Converter.
rules.checks: Each sits in an adapters crate.

rules.title: No technical bucket packages - package by domain concept
rules.rationale: Packages are named after domain concepts from the ubiquitous language, not technical patterns
rules.selects: Every module in the workspace's context crates.
rules.checks: No module is named entities, value_objects, helpers, util or utils.

rules.title: Domain classes must not use technical suffixes (Helper, Util, Impl, Implementation)
rules.rationale: Domain names come from the ubiquitous language - name services by their specialty, not by technical role
rules.selects: Types in every domain crate.
rules.checks: No name ends with Helper, Util, Utils, Impl or Implementation.

rules.title: ViewModels must reside in the configured web adapter package
rules.rationale: A ViewModel is shaped for the protocol of one incoming adapter and belongs in it. It has no reading in the domain or the application layer, and none in a second adapter
rules.selects: Structs whose name ends with ViewModel.
rules.checks: Each sits in the incoming module of an adapters crate, in its configured web submodule.

rules.title: Diagnostic: use cases and input ports named after a trigger rather than an effect
rules.rationale: A use case is named after its effect, never after its trigger or its caller. When and by whom it runs is the business of the adapter or the consumer that calls it; the same effect reached from a second trigger is the same use case, and a name that carries the trigger invites a second use case for it
rules.selects: Input-port traits and use-case types in application crates.
rules.checks: Informational - lists names that contain a trigger word (On, After, When, Upon, Before followed by a capital) and never fails.

rules.title: Use cases, input ports and published operations must not be named after a field they write
rules.rationale: An operation speaks the domain, not data access. A name after the field it writes (setLimit, updateStatus) says how the data changes, not what the change means; the glossary's verb says that (raise a limit, grant an initial limit), and the caller learns which rules run
rules.selects: Input-port traits and use-case types in application crates, and pub functions of api crates.
rules.checks: No type name starts with Set or Update followed by a capital, and no function name starts with set_ or update_.

rules.title: Domain Packages must not have cyclic dependencies (package-based slice discovery)
rules.rationale: Domain model packages should have clear boundaries and no cycles (Acyclic Dependencies Principle)
rules.selects: The domain crates of all contexts.
rules.checks: Cargo refuses a dependency cycle between crates, and DCA-STR-004 refuses any edge between two contexts' domains.

rules.title: Application Layer must not have cyclic dependencies (package-based slice discovery)
rules.rationale: Application services should have clear boundaries and no cycles
rules.selects: The application crates of all contexts.
rules.checks: Cargo refuses a dependency cycle between crates.

rules.title: Outgoing Adapter Packages must not have cyclic dependencies
rules.rationale: Outgoing adapters should have clear boundaries and no cycles
rules.selects: The adapters crates of all contexts.
rules.checks: Cargo refuses a dependency cycle between crates.

rules.title: Incoming Adapter Packages must not have cyclic dependencies
rules.rationale: Incoming adapters should have clear boundaries and no cycles
rules.selects: The adapters crates of all contexts.
rules.checks: Cargo refuses a dependency cycle between crates. Incoming and outgoing adapters of one context share a crate; a cycle between them is DCA-HEX-006's.

rules.title: Feature and use case packages within a module's application layer must not have cyclic dependencies
rules.rationale: The packages directly below a module's application package are its features (application.<feature>.<usecase>) or, in a flat layout, its use cases (application.<usecase>). A feature is an optional, domain-named group of related use cases; it may depend on another feature in one direction, but a cycle between two of them means the grouping does not carry its weight - the shared concept belongs in application.shared, in the domain, or in one of the two. application.shared is the context-wide port package and is not a slice. The rule does not infer bounded contexts or aggregate ownership from the packages it slices
rules.selects: One slice per use-case or feature module of every application crate, the shared module excluded.
rules.checks: The slices form no dependency cycle through use paths. Modules within one crate may depend on each other in both directions; the compiler allows it.

rules.title: Failures declared in the domain layer must implement DomainFailure
rules.rationale: A failure the model raises is a broken business rule and says so through its type; a caller that cannot tell one from the platform's own failures cannot answer either of them properly
rules.selects: Types in every domain crate that implement std::error::Error.
rules.checks: Each implements DomainFailure. Rust has no exceptions; a failure is a type returned in Err.

rules.title: Domain and port exceptions reside in the layer whose failure they name
rules.rationale: The base type states which layer owns the failure; declaring it elsewhere puts the vocabulary of that layer outside it and lets an adapter invent failures the application never reports
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainFailure or a port failure (UseCaseFailure, OutputPortFailure, or the classification traits PortFailure and InputPortFailure).
rules.checks: A DomainFailure sits in a domain crate, a port failure in an application crate - an output port's failure beside the port, although the adapter that implements the port returns it.

rules.title: Failures declared in the application layer must implement UseCaseFailure or OutputPortFailure
rules.rationale: A use case that cannot serve a request reports why through its type, so that one incoming adapter can map each outcome onto its protocol and another adapter can map the same outcome onto a different one; an output port that declares a failure in its contract names it the same way, so the use case can catch exactly that outcome
rules.selects: Types in every application crate that implement std::error::Error and not DomainFailure.
rules.checks: Each implements UseCaseFailure or OutputPortFailure. Implementing only the classification traits PortFailure or InputPortFailure does not count: a type implements the leaf it is.

rules.title: Domain and port exceptions must not carry prohibited framework metadata
rules.rationale: An exception of an inner layer that carries container, persistence or protocol metadata has decided how the outside answers it, which is the incoming adapter's decision and only its; an annotation that fixes the answer's status decides it for every protocol at once, including the ones the exception knows nothing about
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainFailure or a port failure.
rules.checks: None implements a web framework's response trait (for example axum's IntoResponse): the domain and application crates do not depend on the framework, and the orphan rule refuses the impl in the adapters crate, where both trait and type are foreign. The adapter translates through its own type.

rules.title: Domain and port exception names must stay in the language of their layer
rules.rationale: A failure named after a transport concept is a decision about the answer, taken in a layer that does not know the protocol; the name should say what went wrong, not what the caller should be told
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainFailure or a port failure (UseCaseFailure, OutputPortFailure).
rules.checks: The name contains none of Http, StatusCode, ResponseStatus, Response. The suffix part of the Java rule does not apply: Rust names a failure ...Error by convention.

rules.title: Diagnostic: incoming adapter packages that drive a use case without translating its failures
rules.rationale: A package that drives the application and knows neither failure type nor a case of a closed result either lets everything escape to a generic handler or catches a generic type and answers every outcome the same way; whether it does is not visible in the import model. A use case may return its expected refusals as cases of a closed result instead of throwing them; a switch over those cases is the translation then. An adapter that names the abstract base of the port failures catches them generically and answers every outcome the same way
rules.selects: Modules in the incoming part of every adapters crate that name an input port.
rules.checks: Informational - lists a module when no item in it names a DomainFailure or UseCaseFailure type nor a variant of a closed result, and never fails. A closed result is an enum an input-port trait answers with - named in an associated-type binding of its bounds (Output = ...) or in a method's return type, through any wrapper such as Result. A variant counts when a path names it through its enum or through a use of it, so a match over the variants is seen; whether the match is exhaustive is left to the compiler. When the workspace has neither a failure type nor a closed result, nothing is listed. It also lists a module that names one of the classification traits PortFailure, InputPortFailure or OutputPortFailure itself - a bound or a trait object over the base is the generic handler that answers every outcome the same way.

rules.title: Diagnostic: failures that carry display data or objects instead of ids and figures
rules.rationale: A failure carries ids and figures, never what a page shows. Its fields are the typed identities and the values the rule compared; a name or a description of the thing an id refers to is resolved by the translation site through the queries it already has. A failure that carries the name decides for every surface what it shows, and one that carries an aggregate or an entity hands the model out through the error path
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainFailure or a port failure, their fields and variant fields.
rules.checks: Informational - lists every field of type String, an aggregate or an entity, and never fails.

rules.title: Diagnostic: closed use-case results without a case marked as a refusal
rules.rationale: A closed result describes the outcomes a use case can answer with; some of them are refusals, some are not. A result may hold several outcomes of which none refuses - found or nothing found, sent or already sent - and that alone is reason enough to close it. The refusal marker on a case says the request was refused, a meaning the caller answers with or without a transaction, and it is what lets the transaction boundary roll a refusal back like a thrown failure. Whether a case refuses is domain knowledge the type does not show, so a closed result without any marked case is listed for a look, not failed: if one of its outcomes is a refusal and stays unmarked, the transaction commits the writes made before it
rules.selects: Closed results in every application crate: an enum an input-port trait answers with - named in an associated-type binding of its bounds (Output = ...) or in a method's return type, through any wrapper such as Result - as DCA-ERR-006 finds them; an enum that implements std::error::Error, DomainFailure or UseCaseFailure is the failure side and not selected.
rules.checks: Informational - lists every closed result none of whose variants carries a field whose type implements the building-block trait Refusal, and never fails. A unit variant carries nothing and cannot be the refusing one: a refusing variant wraps a value of a type that implements Refusal, and the result enum implements ClosedResult, whose refusal() match the compiler checks for coverage and for the Refusal bound - that is what TransactionBoundary::in_transaction_closed rolls back on. A listed result is not a finding by itself: one whose outcomes are all successes - found or nothing found - is correct as it is. A struct is no closed result.

rules.title: A domain exception is constructed only in the domain layer
rules.rationale: The model refuses: a domain exception names a business rule the model itself broke off. A use case never invents one. A failure the use case finds - an output port returned nothing, the caller does not own what it names, a precondition on a second aggregate - is the application's, a case of its result or a use-case exception; dressed as a domain failure it claims a rule the model never checked, and the model cannot know what a search found
rules.selects: Every expression in a function body of a module outside the domain crates - application, adapters, api, infrastructure, bootstrap and unplaced crates; #[cfg(test)] items and test targets are not read: a struct literal, a call of a tuple struct or an enum variant, a unit struct or unit variant used as a value, a variant or tuple struct passed as a function, and a call of an associated function without a receiver that returns Self or the type itself, whose type implements DomainFailure.
rules.checks: None of them names a domain failure - only a domain crate constructs one. Self is not followed: a domain failure declared outside the domain is DCA-ERR-002's finding. A failure the application only passes on (a variant wrapping it, ? or map_err with a conversion) is not a construction. Constructions inside macro invocations, through From/Into conversions or a generic constructor are not seen. An empty selection passes.

rules.title: The domain holds no shared mutable state
rules.rationale: Rc, Arc, Cell, RefCell, Mutex and RwLock give a value a second owner or a way around &mut. Inside an aggregate they let code outside the root change its parts without the root's invariant check, which is what ownership otherwise prevents.
rules.selects: Every domain crate.
rules.checks: clippy.toml lists std::rc::Rc, std::sync::Arc, std::cell::Cell, std::cell::RefCell, std::sync::Mutex and std::sync::RwLock under disallowed-types; the source test refuses the same types in field types, so a crate without the clippy.toml is held too.

rules.title: Entities compare by identity
rules.rationale: #[derive(PartialEq)] compares every field, which is value equality. Two states of the same entity must be equal and two entities with equal data must not.
rules.selects: Types that implement Entity, aggregate roots included.
rules.checks: The type does not derive PartialEq, Eq or Hash. A manual PartialEq is the expected form; whether it compares only the id is not decidable.

rules.title: Aggregate roots hand out no mutable reference to their parts
rules.rationale: A pub method that returns &mut to an inner entity or collection lets the caller change the aggregate without passing the root's invariant check. Ownership does not prevent it; the signature does.
rules.selects: pub methods of types that implement AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: No return type, through generic arguments, contains a &mut reference.

rules.title: The domain stays synchronous
rules.rationale: Async is an I/O concern of ports and adapters. A synchronous domain stays testable and deterministic and pulls no runtime into the model.
rules.selects: Functions and methods in every domain crate.
rules.checks: None is async and none returns a type that implements Future. A domain crate without a runtime dependency cannot spawn a task either.

rules.title: The domain reads no clock and no randomness
rules.rationale: A domain that reads the time or draws a random number gives different results for the same input, so its tests depend on the moment they run. The value comes in from the application as a parameter.
rules.selects: Every domain crate.
rules.checks: clippy.toml lists std::time::SystemTime::now, std::time::Instant::now, chrono::Utc::now, chrono::Local::now and rand::random under disallowed-methods, and uuid::Uuid::new_v4 and uuid::Uuid::now_v7.

rules.title: An aggregate's event enum carries one event type per variant
rules.rationale: An event is a type of its own, in every DCA language: it can be named, passed, consumed and checked alone (DCA-ADV-001, DCA-ADV-008 per type). An enum gathers an aggregate's events the way a sealed interface lists its records; a variant with inline fields is an event without a type.
rules.selects: Enums that implement DomainEvent.
rules.checks: Every variant has exactly one unnamed field whose type implements DomainEvent and is not the enum itself.
